newsitem.title: USA: US rules against Cemex -- U.S. industry.
newsitem.headline: US rules against Cemex -- U.S. industry.

text.p: The U.S. Commerce Department has made anti-dumping rulings against Mexican cement producer Cemex SA that would cost the company $57 million in duties, a coalition of U.S. cement manufacturers said Tuesday.
Commerce found that Cemex's dumping margin was 109.43 percent from August 1991 to July 1992 and 107.76 percent from August 1994 to July 1995, the Southern Tier Cement Committee said.
If upheld, the two rulings would cost Cemex $32 million for the earlier period and $25 million for the later period, the committee said in a statement.
The Commerce Department informed the Southern Tier Cement Committee of its rulings Monday, committee attorney Joseph Dorn said.
An official at the Commerce Department said no public announcement had been made. The official could not immediately confirm the rulings.
The rulings result from an annual administrative review on imports of Mexican gray portland cement and clinker following an August 1990 anti-dumping order against Mexico.
